summary: Explains idempotency: most modules check the desired state and do nothing if already achieved, so reruns give the same result, but not all modules or playbooks are idempotent.
questions: What does idempotent mean in Ansible?
Is it safe to run a playbook multiple times?

answer_card.title: Desired state and idempotency
answer_card.answer_md: Most modules check whether the desired state already exists and do nothing if so, so running a playbook once or many times gives the same result. Not every module or playbook behaves this way; if unsure, test in a sandbox before repeated production runs.
